T-type Ca(++) currents contribute significantly to the action potential initiation in the olfactory receptor cells during the odorant stimulation.
T-type Ca(+)2 currents enhance the sensitivity of olfactory receptor cells by lowering the threshold for action potential generation.
T-type Ca2+ currents are involved in the generation of odor-evoked action potentials in ORCs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism underlying the initiation of action potentials during odor stimulation in olfactory receptor neurons.
the mechanisms underlying the initiation and propagation of action potential in olfactory receptor neurons.
the role of the T-type Ca2+ current (I(Ca, T)) in the initiation of action potentials in olfactory receptor neurons (ORNs) during odor stimulation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
T-type Ca(+) currents play a major role in the generation of the action potential in olfactory receptor neurons.
I(Ca(T)) contributes to enhance odorant sensitivity by lowering the spike threshold in ORCs.
the T-type Ca(+) channel contributes to the initiation of the action potentials in ORCs, and thus to the odor sensitivity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

I(Ca,L) and I(Nav1.9) play a role in the spike initiation in the soma of ORCs, while I(Ca,T), which is activated by depolarizing current induced by I(Ca,L), contributes to spike initiation in the dendrites of ORCs.
T-type Ca2+ channels play a critical role in the initiation and the generation of action potentials in olfactory receptor neurons.
T-type Ca(+) channels are involved in the initiation and/or propagation of action potentials in ORCs, which are essential for signal transduction in olfactory neurons.
The main takeaway from our work is that
olfactory receptor cells use a T-type calcium current to enhance their sensitivity to odorant molecules.
olfactory receptor cells have a unique mechanism for action potential initiation that is different from other sensory neurons.
T-type calcium currents play a critical role in the initiation of the action potential in olfactory receptor neurons.
